name: bus_listen
description: Use when you need to know whether the CAN bus at the OBD port is alive and which ids talk on it, e.g. modules not answering or network (U) codes.
instructions: Call listen_bus with 1-10 seconds, e.g. {"seconds":5}. It only listens (the adapter's monitor mode); nothing is sent on the bus, and no other reading runs meanwhile.
Use it once per run, after the codes: to check the bus is alive when modules do not answer, or to see which ids talk when there are network (U) codes.
Read the frame count and the number of distinct ids first, then the busiest ids and their frames per second.
interpret: Frames from several ids at steady rates mean the bus at the OBD port is alive.

No frames at all: the OBD port may sit behind a gateway that passes only diagnostic traffic (many VAG cars of this era), the ignition may be off, or the adapter cannot monitor this bus. That alone is not a fault.
On VAG cars with the gateway in front of the OBD port, the ids heard are mostly diagnostic traffic (7E0 / 7E8, 200 / 2xx TP2.0 setup), not the powertrain bus: do not read them as module broadcasts.
An id is an arbitration id, not a module name: say which id is busy, never guess which module sends it.
Frames per second here are an average over a few seconds; a short listen does not prove an intermittent bus fault is absent.
Unparsed lines (BUFFER FULL and similar) mean the adapter could not keep up with the bus: frames around them are missing, so counts are a lower bound.
